milestone: Horizen Pilot — Aigent Nakamoto live registration
problem: Nakamoto was registered on base-sepolia (tx 0xedda5f73…, tokenId 8798) and the platform could not see it. The registration-binding resolver reported 'not registered' every time, so the Register ladder, the Agent Card and the Verify stage each answered differently about one fact. Repair spanned 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-03 and took several cycles because each fix exposed the next observer reading a different source.
observedFailure: The legacy receipt lacked a structured registration.tokenId block, so the receipt fallback skipped it as malformed — the exact receipt the fallback existed to rescue.

Receipt lookup used the agent handle (personas.fio_handle = 'nakamoto@aigent') although the receipt belonged to the OPERATOR persona that acted; the query searched a structurally empty set every time.

A test explicitly asserted legacy receipts should be ignored — titled 'ignores a receipt with no structured registration block' and fed exactly the shape of Nakamoto's real receipt. The defect was specified, asserted and defended by a green test.
rootCauses: A receipt is written with personaId = the ACTING operator, and the subject of the receipt is a different reference (the registered agent). The lookup keyed on the wrong one of the two.
A schema enrichment (the structured `registration` block) was introduced in the same change as the fallback that read it, so the fallback could only read data that did not yet exist in production.
The binding-resolver test file mocked the author's beliefs rather than the system's data — six tests passed while the resolver could never work.
resolution: Added `findAgentRegistrationReceipts` to the canonical receipt service — subject-keyed on `agents_invoked`, returning only the narrow facts asked for, never the persona-scoped receipt body.

Where a legacy record carries less, recover the rest from a source that can still be interrogated: decode the registration transaction the receipt names, bounded by an owner check, refusing rather than guessing when the chain does not confirm it.
Rewrote tests/horizen-agent-registration-binding.test.ts against real evidence — Nakamoto's actual tx hash, tokenId, registry address and wallet are fixture constants at the top of the file.
Gave the ladder a single precedence order so one screen gives one answer (OS-1/OS-2/OS-3).
rejectedApproaches: Treat the operator wallet as the agent identifier — a wallet is the OWNER reference, not the agent reference; ERC-721 gives no reverse (wallet → tokenId) enumeration guarantee, so this could answer confidently and wrongly.
Query the database directly outside the canonical receipt service — a second reader of one fact is a second observer that will eventually disagree.
Ignore pre-enrichment receipts — that is the failure, restated as a policy.
